title: OOA
body:
**Object Oriented Analysis.** Find the objects in the *problem*. Read the requirements, pull
out the nouns that have both data and behaviour, and work out how they relate. The output
describes the domain, not the software: an OOA model of a library says there are books,
borrowers, and loans, and says nothing about Java, databases, or screens.

## OOA vs OOD vs OOM, which is the thing to actually keep straight

The three are one pipeline and the acronyms blur, so this note holds the distinction and
[[OOD]] and [[OOM]] point back here rather than restating it.

| | Question | Lives in | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| **OOA** | what objects exist in the problem? | the domain | domain object model |
| **[[OOD]]** | what classes will implement them? | the solution | class design, interfaces |
| **[[OOM]]** | how do we draw either of the above? | notation | the diagrams |

The line between OOA and OOD is **problem versus solution**. Analysis is allowed to talk
about a `Loan` because the library has loans; design is where `LoanRepository`,
`DueDateCalculator`, and everything else that exists only because software exists get added.
OOM is not a third stage at all: it is the notation both use, which is why it appears
alongside them instead of after them.

Mapping onto the [[SDLC]]: OOA belongs to [[Software Requirements Analysis]], OOD belongs to
[[Design]].

## Finding objects

The rough heuristic: nouns in the requirements are candidate objects, verbs are candidate
operations on them, and adjectives are candidate attributes. It is a starting point rather
than a method. Most candidate nouns are not objects, and the ones that survive are the ones
that have state *and* behaviour, and that would still be recognisable to a librarian who has
never seen the code.

A domain object that matches something real is the one that stays stable while requirements
change, which is the whole bet the [[Object Oriented Approach]] makes against the
[[Structured Approach]]: functions change, things do not.

Related: [[Abstraction]], [[Object]], [[Classes]], [[Encapsulation]].
